two of your papers with you, Michael Levin, have been published with your co-authors,
which are here, Gizem Gomeskaya and Angela Tung. So Michael, I'd like you to explain what these

those papers. So Michael, please. Yeah, sure. Yeah, it's really interesting to me that these

here. One, so Gizem's has to do with something we call anthrobots, which are these, it's a new

to together solve the problem of morphogenesis better than individuals or small groups. And so in both
cases, it's this really interesting dynamic of where biological control information comes from.
All right, great. Gizem, if you don't mind, please, what is the significance of that?

shift in our thinking about biology and nature. We tend to think about nature as this thing sitting

these cells to create a new architecture that we had designed a priori. So yeah, like in summary,
they are the first sort of fully cellular living, self-constructing biological robots,

Okay. Yeah. I mean, that's actually, that's a really important point. Because when we made the
